gaussian_evaluation.dx: __hsub2(__low2half2(xy_mt_j), offset_x)  // gaussian_mean_x - pixel_x, in half2, 2 pixels per __half2
gaussian_evaluation.dy: __hsub2(mean_y, offset_y[pp])  // gaussian_mean_y - pixel_y, in half2, 2 pixels per __half2
gaussian_evaluation.conic_source: smem_conic_raw[idx] — Cholesky factors (l00, l10, l11, l22) scaled by CHOL_SCALE=0.8493*16=13.589, with -log2(opac) fused into the 4th half slot
gaussian_evaluation.exp_implementation: __h2exp2_approx(__hneg2(sigma)) — half2 approximate base-2 exponential (CUDA hardware MUFU.EX2 via half2 intrinsic)
gaussian_evaluation.sigma_fusion: sigma = __hfma2(u1,u1, __hfma2(u0,u0, neg_log_opac)) — single FMA chain, no separate multiply
gaussian_evaluation.threshold_in_sigma_domain: ok_mask = __hlt2_mask(sigma, sigma_thresh) where sigma_thresh = log2(1/ALPHA_THRESHOLD) = log2(255) = 7.9943534f
gaussian_evaluation.note: The q(x,y) in the spec corresponds to 'sigma' in code: sigma = u0^2 + u1^2 - log2(opac). exp2(-sigma) = opac * exp2(-(u0^2+u1^2)) = full gaussian weight including opacity.

alpha_semantics.opacity_gaussian_product: Fused: exp2(-sigma) where sigma includes -log2(opac). Result = opac * exp2(-(u0^2+u1^2)). No separate multiply.
alpha_semantics.alpha_clamp: NOT explicitly clamped to MAX_ALPHA in forward kernel. The threshold test (sigma < log2(1/AT)) effectively bounds alpha < 1.0. MAX_ALPHA=0.99 clamp is only in RasterizeToPixels3DGSDevice.cuh (shared code, used by backward).
alpha_semantics.alpha_threshold: ALPHA_THRESHOLD = 1/255 ≈ 0.003922. In sigma domain: sigma_thresh = log2(255) = 7.9943534f. Pixels with sigma >= 7.994 are rejected (alpha < 1/255).
alpha_semantics.alpha_reject: ok_mask = __hlt2_mask(sigma, sigma_thresh); alpha_ht = __h2if(ok_mask, alpha, 0.0f) — sub-threshold pixels get alpha=0, contribute nothing
alpha_semantics.transmittance_termination: acc[pp][3] = __hsub2_sat(acc[pp][3], vis) where vis = alpha_ht * T. MIN_TRANSPARENCY = 1e-4f. Per-pair done mask: __hlt2_mask(acc_T, 1e-4). Warp-wide exit: __ballot_sync(~0u, tile_done == DONE_MASK) == ~0u → break.
alpha_semantics.max_alpha: MAX_ALPHA = 0.99f (Common.h:105, used only in backward via RasterizeToPixels3DGSDevice.cuh)

thread_pixel_mapping.full_coverage: Each lane covers 8 pixels: (thread_x, thread_y + 0..7). Warp covers 32*8 = 256 = 16x16 tile. ✓

raster_loop_structure.queue_fill: Per mini-batch (32 gaussians): each lane checks if its gaussian overlaps this tile (smem_masks[mb*32 + tile_idx] bit lane_id). If yes, computes pos = popc(mask & ((1<<lane)-1)) and writes warp_queue[write_head + pos] = mb*32 + lane_id. write_head += popc(mask). All lanes see the same mask → warp builds a contiguous index list of gaussians overlapping this tile.
raster_loop_structure.drain_loop: Drains 32-entry batches from warp_queue. UNROLL_FACTOR=8: loads 8 consecutive queue indices via uint4 batched LDS, calls rasterizeGaussian 8 times. Tail loop handles remaining < 8.
raster_loop_structure.early_exit: After each drain batch: per-pair done mask (T < 1e-4). If ALL 8 pixel pairs are done for ALL 32 lanes (ballot == ~0u), break out of the entire raster loop for this tile.

backward_kernel.name: higs_blend_bwd_px_kernel<3, 2, true, true>
backward_kernel.warp_mapping: warp_w covers rows [2w, 2w+1] of the 16x16 tile (PX_ROWS=8, ty ∈ {0..7}, pixels at ty and ty+8)
backward_kernel.lane_mapping: lane l → column j = tile_x_base + l (one pixel per lane per q-pixel, 2 q-pixels per lane)

gaussian_evaluation.function: eval_gaussian_weight(conic, dx, dy, opac) at RasterizeToPixels3DGSDevice.cuh:44-55
gaussian_evaluation.sigma: 0.5 * (conic.x*dx^2 + conic.z*dy^2) + conic.y*dx*dy (FP32, full conic, not Cholesky)
gaussian_evaluation.exp_implementation: __expf(-sigma) — CUDA fast FP32 exponential (MUFU.EX2 via __expf intrinsic)
gaussian_evaluation.note: Backward uses full FP32 conic (A,B,C form), NOT the half2 Cholesky form used by forward. Different numerical path but same mathematical quantity.

lockstep.mechanism: All 256/PX = 128 threads (4 warps) in the CTA iterate the same gaussian at index t (batched via smem). Each thread evaluates the gaussian at its own pixel(s). Warp reduction (cg::reduce warpSum) then atomicAdd scatters to global.
lockstep.proof: HigsNativeBackward.cu:468 (for t loop): conic_batch[t], xy_opacity_batch[t], rgbs_batch[t*CDIM] are indexed by t which is identical for all threads in the CTA. The per-pixel variation is only in px[q], py[q] (thread-specific pixel coords).
lockstep.source_lines: HigsNativeBackward.cu:446-583 (px kernel main loop), 468 (t loop), 485-489 (per-q eval with same conic_batch[t])

gradient_scatter.warp_reduction: warpSum(v_rgb_local, warp) + warpSum(v_conic_local, warp) + warpSum(v_xy_local, warp) + warpSum(v_opacity_local, warp) via cooperative_groups::reduce
gradient_scatter.atomic_scatter: warp.thread_rank()==0 does atomicAdd to v_colors[g*3+k], v_conics[3g+k], v_means2d[2g+k], v_opacities[g] (lines 558-581)
gradient_scatter.scatter_type: gather (per-pixel) → warp reduce → single atomicAdd per gaussian per warp per iteration
gradient_scatter.note: NOT a per-pixel scatter. The warp reduction collapses 32 pixel contributions into one set of gradient values per gaussian, then a single lane does the atomic.

forward.smem_xy_mt: __half2 per gaussian [FUSED_GAUSS_BATCH_SIZE=1024] — gaussian position in tile units relative to macro-tile center
forward.smem_conic_raw: uint2 per gaussian [1024] — 4x half: {l00, l10, l11, -log2(opac)} scaled by CHOL_SCALE
forward.smem_color: ushort4 per gaussian [1024] — 4x fp16: {R, G, B, _} packed from [N,4] half layout
forward.smem_masks: uint32 per (mini_batch, tile) [32*32=1024] — per-tile gaussian overlap masks
forward.loading: Phase 1: lane j loads gaussian j from global (means2d, conics) → smem. Colors: full CTA strided load (threadIdx.x, stride blockDim.x).

can_add_k_exp_dd.analysis: Add 2 bytes (one half) per gaussian to smem_conic_raw (make it uint3) or add a separate __half[1024] array. Total additional: 2048 bytes. Total smem: 16524+2048 = 18572 bytes. Well within 100KB shared memory limit (sm_80). The k=exp(dd) value is per-gaussian, computed once in Phase 1 (same location where conic and -log2(opac) are already computed), and read once per gaussian in Phase 2 rasterizeGaussian. No additional global memory traffic — dd is already in registers during Phase 1 conic processing.

backward.loading: Each thread loads 1 gaussian from global (flatten_ids, means2d, conics, opacities, colors) into smem. block.sync() before processing.

can_add_k_exp_dd.analysis: Add a float[128] k_batch array (512 bytes) or float[2] per gaussian packed into xy_opacity. dd comes from the depth buffer (or can be computed from conic/means). Additional global traffic: 1 float per gaussian per batch load. smem: +512 bytes (negligible).

forward_tile16.lockstep_mechanism: All 32 lanes in a warp read the same b_idx[i] from warp_queue (uniform LDS). rasterizeGaussian is called with identical gaussian index but per-lane pixel coordinates (px, py). No per-lane divergence in gaussian selection.
forward_tile16.proof: MacroTileRasterize.cu:554-559 — b_idx loaded via uint4 LDS (4x uint16) from warp_queue[base+q]. All 32 lanes execute the same LDG → same b_idx values → same gaussian index. The per-lane variation is ONLY in the pixel coordinates (offset_x, offset_y derived from lane_id). No __shfl, no per-lane branch on gaussian selection.
divergence_sources: Early exit (tile_done == DONE_MASK): when ALL lanes saturate, the warp breaks. Before that, all lanes process the same gaussians. Partial saturation (some pixels done, some not) does NOT cause per-lane divergence in gaussian processing — the done mask only triggers exit when ALL pixels in ALL pairs are done for ALL lanes.
Alpha threshold (ok_mask): sub-threshold pixels get alpha=0 but still participate in the FMA (contributing 0). No branch divergence.
forward_tile16.conclusion: f_lockstep = 1.0 for all W ∈ {4, 8, 16}. Every iteration of the drain loop processes the same gaussian across all 32 lanes.

backward_px2.lockstep_mechanism: All 128 threads (4 warps) in the CTA iterate the same gaussian at index t. conic_batch[t], xy_opacity_batch[t], rgbs_batch[t*3] are shared (smem), indexed by the same t for all threads. Per-thread variation is only in pixel coordinates (px[q], py[q]).
backward_px2.proof: HigsNativeBackward.cu:468 (for t loop) — t is the loop variable, identical for all threads. Lines 485-489: conic_batch[t], xy_opacity_batch[t] are smem loads with uniform index t. Lines 489: eval_gaussian_weight called with same conic/opac but per-pixel delta. No per-lane branch on gaussian index.
divergence_sources: valid[q] per-pixel: some pixels may be invalid (outside image, or gaussian below threshold). But the t loop continues for all threads — invalid pixels just contribute 0 to the warp reduction. No early exit per-lane within the t loop.
warp.any(valid) check (line 486/546): if ALL lanes in a warp are invalid, the iteration is skipped (continue). But this is warp-uniform — all lanes skip together. No per-lane divergence.
backward_px2.conclusion: f_lockstep = 1.0 for all W ∈ {4, 8, 16}. Every iteration of the t loop processes the same gaussian across all threads in the CTA (and thus all lanes in any warp).

forward_backward_mapping_compatibility.explanation: Forward: lane l → (x=l%16, y=l/16) within a 16x16 tile, each lane covers 8 pixel rows (pairs). Backward PX=2: warp w, lane l → column j=l, rows {2w, 2w+1, 2w+8, 2w+9}. Different mapping. However, this does NOT affect lockstep — both are 'same gaussian across all lanes' patterns.
forward_backward_mapping_compatibility.qscan_compatibility: QSCAN can reuse the same subgroup mapping in both forward and backward because the lockstep property (same gaussian index across lanes) is identical. The per-lane pixel coordinate mapping differs, but QSCAN operates on the gaussian-level reduction (k=exp(dd) per gaussian), not the per-pixel coordinate.

qscan_feasibility.forward: QSCAN4/8/16 all have f_lockstep=1.0. QSCAN can be applied at any subgroup width. The per-gaussian k=exp(dd) can be cooperatively loaded to smem in Phase 1 (alongside conic, xy, color) with zero additional global traffic.
qscan_feasibility.backward: QSCAN4/8/16 all have f_lockstep=1.0. Same cooperative load pattern applies in the backward batch load phase.
qscan_feasibility.reasoning: Since f_lockstep=1.0 for all widths, the maximum W=16 is feasible. W=16 gives the best amortization of the per-gaussian k load across 16 lanes. The subgroup mapping is compatible between forward and backward.
